# ADR-0013: Turn result contract — structured state back from turn pods

> **Status:** proposed | **Date:** 2026-07-06

**References:** [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md)

## Context

Turn pods return everything via stdout markers scraped from kube logs. Six marker literals are duplicated across crates with "keep in sync" comments. 2026-07-05 production incidents exposed fragility: openshell event stream glued messages breaking parse contracts; payloads fight kubelet's 10 MiB log-rotation budget; binary artifacts ride logs as base64; markers duplicate across a crate DAG that forbids sharing. The OTLP collector was lost when vendored agentic-ci was dropped, and harness logic was trapped in a binary.

## Decision

Two-tier result contract in a shared crucible-contract crate. Tier 1: verdict rides the Kubernetes termination message (4096 B, self-capped at 3584 B). Tier 2: artifacts POST to the controller's evidence drop-box via an authenticated endpoint (pod-bound projected SA token validated by TokenReview). Stdout demotes to a human-facing live/debug channel. The crucible-harness crate is extracted as the agentic-ci replacement; the OTLP collector is restored in-process.

## Consequences

Positive: verdict path stops depending on log rotation, newline discipline, or base64-in-logs. Scope turns survive controller downtime. Artifact caps become honest HTTP limits. Six keep-in-sync literal pairs collapse into one typed crate (crucible-contract). Authoritative cost returns to the ledger. Harness becomes a consumable crate.

Negative: requires a controller endpoint and projected SA token infrastructure. Two transport tiers add operational complexity versus the single-channel stdout approach.

## Alternatives Considered

### Two-tier result contract: verdict in termination message (4096 B), artifacts via authenticated HTTP POST to controller evidence drop-box (accepted)


### Continue using stdout markers scraped from kube logs for all result communication (rejected)
